newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends weak but off early lows.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends weak but off early lows.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended weak on Friday but above six-month lows seen earlier in the session as traders booked profits on short positions and U.S. products steadied, dealers said.
April Brent closed at $19.82 a barrel, down 26 cents from Thursday but six cents off the intraday low of $19.76 a barrel. Prompt Brent last traded at that level on August 9.
Brokers said a combination of technical support, short-covering after this week's 67-cent losses and steady U.S. heating oil provided a prop to Brent crude in late dealing after an early slide.
"Technical support held and (NYMEX) heating also helped underpin Brent," said one.
Chartists saw support at $19.75 a barrel, where the bottom of a six-week downtrend channel crosses, and then at $19.70, another previous low from last August.
Despite the steady close, brokers were wary of predicting an end to a slide which has knocked nearly $5 off Brent since the start of the year as heating oil demand waned and supply surged.
On Thursday, the United Nations approved Iraq's request to offer special discounts on its Basrah Light crude exports to the United States, which have struggled to find buyers.
Earlier, IPE gas oil futures confirmed a rare midwinter shift into contango by sliding $3 a tonne, pressured by mild temperatures in both Europe and Northeastern United States, traders said.
Front month March finished at $170.50 after hitting a seven-month, spot contract low of $169.75.
March extended Thursday's 25-cent contango, settling $1 below the second month contract. May finished at $172.25.
"It's the mild weather, no German buying and the movement in the dollar preventing buyers getting into the market," a trader said. --Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
